        ### Question
        An autopsy is being performed on an elderly man who died from a myocardial infarction. Biopsy of the heart is likely to reveal necrosis most similar to necrosis seen in which of the following scenarios?

        ### Options
        opa. The central nervous system following a stroke
opb. The lung following a tuberculosis infection
opc. Acute pancreatitis resulting from release of enzymatically active enzymes into the pancreas
opd. A region of kidney where blood flow is obstructed
ope. An abscess

### Reasoning Chains per Option:
CHAIN: Myocardial infarction -> ischemic injury to the heart tissue -> necrosis in the heart muscle -> 80% CHAIN: Necrosis in the heart muscle -> coagulative necrosis -> similar to necrosis seen in a region of the kidney where blood flow is obstructed -> 75% CHAIN: Myocardial infarction -> ischemic injury to the heart tissue -> necrosis in the heart muscle -> similar to necrosis seen in acute pancreatitis due to enzymatic activity -> 80%

### Retrieved Evidence Paths (broad but correct):

(Necrosis)-MANIFESTATION_OF->(Pathogenesis)-MANIFESTATION_OF->(Pancreatitis, Acute)
(Heart tissue)-LOCATION_OF->(Disease)-CAUSES/COMPLICATES->(Necrosis)
(Myocardium)-LOCATION_OF->(Necrosis)
